incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: KMS Decrypt error spike detected for customer-facing inference traffic in us-west-2. 429s and 'KeyNotFound' returned from KMS. Alert group: kms-decrypt-high-rate.

pagerduty-bot: Incident created (INC-2026-847). Initial impact: ~8% 429s on generation endpoints, concentrated on routes using key alias 'rw-inference-prod-v1'. Paging on-call.

ben: acked. I'm on it. Seeing a sudden bump in KMS throttling metrics in CloudWatch plus a small number of 'KeyNotFound' traces. Not sure if it's a canonical rotation or HSM flake.

sara: I'm pulling last 24h key rotation events from the control plane. Quick check: no org-initiated rotation for that alias in the last 48h.

alex: Paste of recent decrypt errors from logs: 
```
2026-03-14T18:33:02Z ERROR decrypt failed key=alias/rw-inference-prod-v1 err=KeyNotFound
2026-03-14T18:33:03Z WARN decrypt retry count=1 status=429
2026-03-14T18:33:04Z ERROR decrypt failed key=alias/rw-inference-prod-v1 err=ServiceUnavailable
```

maya: Noted customer reports of elevated latencies. I can open a high-level impact snapshot for support: which customers are hitting that alias the most?

ben: quick hit: two large customers in us-west-2 saw 15-20% request failures; others ~2-3%. Cache hit rate for KV prefix cache dropped slightly (maybe because of error paths).

sara: Control plane audit shows an automated key rewrap job started 18:32:58 UTC targeting alias/rw-inference-prod-v1 across regions. It reports a partial failure in us-west-2: HSM returned transient errors and a subset of key versions did not finish rewrapping. Looks like a partial/failed rotation attempt.

ben: ok, hypothesis: rewrap/rotation attempted and partially applied -> some hosts have new key version metadata, others still reference old version -> KMS returns KeyNotFound for mismatched requests, and retry storms cause throttling. Immediate mitigation: pause the rewrap job and pin services to last-known-good key version. Also trigger vendor escalation.

alex: Executing pause: `kubectl -n infra exec job/auto-key-rewrap -- /bin/stop` -> job reported SIGTERM and is in Terminating state. Posting logs: 
```
Stopping rewrap job id=rw-job-613
Flush in-flight: 54 tasks
Job paused by operator
```

hsm-vendor-oncall: Thanks for the heads up. We're seeing increased latency inside the HSM cluster for that partition in us-west-2 caused by a firmware-backed GC sweep. We're putting the partition in maintenance mode to prevent further partial writes. ETA 14 minutes.

maya: Good. While vendor mitigates, we should fallback to cached wrapped keys to reduce KMS calls. Can we enable temporary local key cache bypass TTL extension?

ben: I can flip the config on the inference pool to use 'key_cache_ttl_seconds=3600' instead of 60. Doing a rolling config push to a small canary: 
```
PATCH /config/pools/inference-canary
{"key_cache_ttl_seconds":3600}
```
Applied to 5% of hosts. Monitoring for error decrease.

sara: Also starting a targeted rollback of metadata for services that recently picked up new key refs. Running a diffsync between metadata-store and kms-metadata-backup. If we detect mismatch, will rebind to backup version.

pagerduty-bot: INC-2026-847 acknowledged by ben. Escalation policy: if not resolved in 15m, will page security and platform oncall.

alex: Canary results: on the hosts with TTL increase, 429s dropped from 18% -> 4% within 90s. Good short-term.

ben: Requesting support team to notify customers in the affected list with an incident banner. Maya, can you draft? Keep it minimal: degradations in generation latency and intermittent failures; mitigation in progress; ETA for resolution ~30m.

maya: Drafted and posted to status.redwood.com as incident KMS-DECRYPT-USW2. I'll ping support channel.

hsm-vendor-oncall: Maintenance mode stopped further writes; background GC running slowly, we're replaying pending rewraps. Expected full recovery of partition metadata in 12-18 minutes.

sara: Rebind script is halfway through; 47 of 92 services reconciled to the backup key version. I'm pausing reconciliation for high-traffic services to avoid spikes.

ben: Next steps: 1) keep TTL increase for 1h, 2) complete rebind for remaining services, 3) coordinate with vendor for post-mortem and firmware fix, 4) revert any automated rewrap jobs until we have stronger pre-checks.

alex: Running `redis-cli --scan --pattern \"keymeta:alias/rw-inference-prod-v1*\"` shows some hosts still have stale pointers. I'll nuke stale pointers only after we confirm backup mapping. Proceeding cautiously.

pagerduty-bot: 10 minutes elapsed. No further PD escalations.

maya: Support has sent initial customer notices and opened follow-ups for the two largest affected customers. One requested SLA credit estimation; finance + acct team looped in.

ben: We're seeing error rates back to normal baseline ~0.5% and the 'KeyNotFound' traces spiking down. HSM vendor reports partition healthy again.

hsm-vendor-oncall: Partition fully recovered. We'll handoff to firmware team for GC tuning to avoid future in-maintenance surprises.

sara: Rewrap job remains paused and will require a safe-run checklist before re-enabling: pre-check that all hosts have consistent metadata, canaries in two regions, and vendor clearance. I'm creating a runbook PR now.

ben: Great work everyone. I'll close the PD incident once we have the post-mortem outline. For on-call handoff: I'm handing off to alex for the follow-up action list and IMMEDIATE tasks. Alex, you're on-call owner for the post-incident.

alex: ack. I'll own the follow-up and schedule a postmortem with vendor. Adding timeline notes and snippets to the incident doc.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-847 status: resolved (mitigated). Postmortem requested.

ben: closing the thread here. Big takeaway: block automated rewrap triggers during high utilization windows and add preflight verification for HSM partition readiness.

maya: Leaving a quick retrospective note: customers appreciated timely notices; need a templated SLA calculator for quick reply.

alex: will add to action items. Closing now.
